l-e-e3-b05-31.title: Di order for writing daily routine
l-e-e3-b05-31.goal: Compare two ways of writing daily routine, choose di one wey fit better, and explain your reason.
l-e-e3-b05-31.material: I get up at seven. I eat lunch at noon. I go to bed at nine. You dey arrange daily routine. A: Write according to di earliest time. B: Write according to di shortest sentence.
l-e-e3-b05-31.s.s1.o.a: A: Di order of time show how di day dey go
l-e-e3-b05-31.s.s1.r.b: If di order different, di way di day dey go go confuse.
l-e-e3-b05-31.s.s1.o.c: B: Short sentences dey easy to read
l-e-e3-b05-31.s.s1.r.c: If na according to shortness, di way di day dey go go disappear.
l-e-e3-b05-31.s.s1.o.d: A: Di time order hard, so I no go use am
l-e-e3-b05-31.s.s1.r.d: Di standard no be whether e hard, but whether e show how di day dey go.
l-e-e3-b05-31.s.s1.explain: Daily routine na how one day dey go. If you write according to earliest time, you go see wetin happen first and wetin happen later.
l-e-e3-b05-31.s.s2.model.0: Writing according to time show how di day dey go, so A fit pass.
l-e-e3-b05-31.s.s2.model.1: If you write according to sentence length, wetin happen first and wetin happen later go mix up, so B no good way to write daily routine.

l-e-e3-b05-32.title: W na two U?
l-e-e3-b05-32.goal: Compare two claims about letter W, choose di one wey fit better, and explain your reason.
l-e-e3-b05-32.material: Dem dey call W double-u (two U). A: Dem write W with two U, so na two letters. B: W na one letter, and na only di name be double-u.
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s1.o.a: A: W na U wey dem write two times
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s1.r.a: W na one letter wey you write at once.
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s1.o.b: A: Di name get two U, so na two letters
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s1.r.b: Name different from shape. W na one letter.
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s1.o.c: B: W na letter wey no get name
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s1.r.c: W get name too; dem dey call am double-u.
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s1.o.d: B: Di name na double-u, and di letter na one
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s1.explain: W na one letter, and double-u na di name of dat letter. Even if di name get U two times, dat no make two letters.
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s2.model.0: W na one letter wey you write at once, and na only di name be double-u, so B fit better.
l-e-e3-b05-32.s.s2.model.1: Name and shape different, so even if di name get two U, na only one letter.

l-e-e3-b05-33.title: Bag and bug dey rhyme?
l-e-e3-b05-33.goal: Compare two claims about wetin make words rhyme, choose di one wey fit better, and explain your reason.
l-e-e3-b05-33.material: A: bag and bug get same first and last sounds, so dem rhyme. B: To rhyme, di sounds must be same from middle vowel reach di end. Di vowels for bag and bug different.
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s1.o.a: A: Di beginning and end na same, so e rhyme
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s1.r.a: Di middle vowels different, so di sounds no match.
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s1.o.b: A: If di first sound na same, e rhyme
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s1.r.b: For rhyme, no be di first sound but di ending sounds suppose be same.
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s1.o.c: B: E suppose be same from vowel reach di end
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s1.o.d: B: If any sound na same, e rhyme
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s1.r.d: No be any sound at all, na from vowel reach di end.
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s1.explain: To rhyme, di sounds suppose be same from vowel reach di end. Bag and bug get different vowels, so dem no rhyme.
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s2.model.0: Di middle vowels for bag and bug different, so di sounds no match, wey make B claim fit better.
l-e-e3-b05-33.s.s2.model.1: Words rhyme only when dem be same from vowel reach di end, like cat and hat, so bag and bug, wey only share first and last sounds, no rhyme.

l-e-e3-b05-34.title: If e get tired, e be past?
l-e-e3-b05-34.goal: Compare two ways to know past sentences, choose di one wey fit better, and explain your reason.
l-e-e3-b05-34.material: I am tired now. talk about something wey dey happen now. A: If word end with -ed, na past sentence. B: Look at time words like now together with verb form.
l-e-e3-b05-34.s.s1.r.a: Some words end with -ed but no be past.
l-e-e3-b05-34.s.s1.o.b: B: You no need look time words
l-e-e3-b05-34.s.s1.o.c: B: now tell you say na present
l-e-e3-b05-34.s.s1.o.d: A: tired end with -ed, so na past
l-e-e3-b05-34.s.s1.r.d: Tired mean “feeling worn out,” and now tell you say na present.
l-e-e3-b05-34.s.s1.explain: Tired mean “feeling worn out,” and am and now tell you say na present. B, wey look time word and verb together, na di one wey fit.
l-e-e3-b05-34.s.s2.model.0: Now tell you say na present, so B, wey look time word and verb together, fit better.
l-e-e3-b05-34.s.s2.model.1: Tired talk about condition wey dey now even though e end with -ed, so A, wey only look -ed, wrong.

l-e-e3-b05-35.title: How you go answer about something wey no dey for text?
l-e-e3-b05-35.goal: Compare two ways to answer question about something wey no dey for text, choose di one wey fit better, and explain your reason.
l-e-e3-b05-35.material: Rui get ball. E blue. Question: Rui like di ball? Di text no talk whether Rui like am. A: Rui probably like am, so answer Yes. B: E no dey for text, so talk say you no fit know.
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s1.o.a: A: Rui get ball, so Rui like am
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s1.r.a: Di text no ever talk say to get ball mean to like am.
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s1.o.b: A: Everybody like dem, so na Yes
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s1.r.b: You no suppose decide by yourself about something wey no dey for text.
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s1.o.c: B: Use only wetin dey for text as your evidence
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s1.o.d: B: Answer without reading di text
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s1.r.d: You gats read di text and find evidence.
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s1.explain: All di text talk na say di ball blue. Something wey no dey for text no get evidence, so you talk say you no fit know.
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s2.model.0: Di text no talk say Rui like am, so B, wey use only wetin dey inside di text as evidence, fit better.
l-e-e3-b05-35.s.s2.model.1: “Yes” na guess wey text no mention, so B, wey answer say you no fit know, correct.

l-e-e3-b06-31.title: Where alphabet middle dey?
l-e-e3-b06-31.goal: Compare two methods or claims about middle of 26 alphabet letters, choose the better one and explain why.
l-e-e3-b06-31.material: Alphabet get 26 letters. K: Middle na exactly one letter. L: Middle dey between two letters. The 13th letter from front na M.
l-e-e3-b06-31.s.s1.o.a: K: 26 odd, so one middle dey.
l-e-e3-b06-31.s.s1.o.b: K: Middle letter na only M.
l-e-e3-b06-31.s.s1.r.b: 12 letters dey before M and 13 after, so e no be middle.
l-e-e3-b06-31.s.s1.o.c: L: Middle dey between A and Z.
l-e-e3-b06-31.s.s1.r.c: A and Z na first and last letters.
l-e-e3-b06-31.s.s1.o.d: L: E na 13 + 13, so e dey between M and N.
l-e-e3-b06-31.s.s1.explain: The 26 letters split to two groups of 13. Front group end at M and back group start at N, so middle dey between M and N.
l-e-e3-b06-31.s.s2.model.0: 26 split as 13 + 13, so claim L, say middle dey between M and N, better.
l-e-e3-b06-31.s.s2.model.1: 26 even, so one middle letter no fit dey; this mean K wrong.

l-e-e3-b06-32.goal: Compare two methods or claims about pronoun wey go in subject position, choose the better one and explain why.
l-e-e3-b06-32.material: Pat and ___ play ball. A: Use me. B: Use I. The people wey dey play ball na Pat and me, the speaker.
l-e-e3-b06-32.s.s1.o.a: B: Pat come first, so use I.
l-e-e3-b06-32.s.s1.r.a: Na role as person doing action, no be order, dey decide say I correct.
l-e-e3-b06-32.s.s1.o.b: B: E dey position of person doing action, so use I.
l-e-e3-b06-32.s.s1.r.c: The standard no be how soft e sound, but its role in sentence.
l-e-e3-b06-32.s.s1.o.d: A: E dey receiving position, so use me.
l-e-e3-b06-32.s.s1.r.d: Dem na people wey dey play ball. Dem no dey receive.
l-e-e3-b06-32.s.s1.explain: Use I for position of people wey dey play ball. For receiving place use me, like Give it to me.
l-e-e3-b06-32.s.s2.model.0: Na position of person doing the action, so B, wey use I, better.
l-e-e3-b06-32.s.s2.model.1: Me na word for receiving side, so I correct for blank where person dey do action.
